newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain farmers estimate 70-80 bln ptas flood damage.
newsitem.headline: Spain farmers estimate 70-80 bln ptas flood damage.

text.p: Flooding after heavy rain in Spain's southern region of Andalusia has caused damage of around 70-80 billion pesetas to crops so far, the farmers' association ASAJA estimated on Tuesday.
Government agriculture officials in Madrid or Andalusia were unavailable for comment.

"The damage is really significant with the majority of cultivated land flooded. Between Cadiz, Huelva and Seville there's about 70,000 hectares which are affected...that could be around 70-80 billion pesetas' worth," said Felipe Gallo, a spokesman for ASAJA in Seville.
He estimated that around 10-15 percent of the olive crop might be lost altogether, with damage estimated at around 30-35 billion pesetas.
"Apart from that you have to take into account the loss of quality in the crop salvaged," Gallo added.
He estimated around 10-12 billion pesetas worth of losses in soft and durum wheat crops.
"There's also the fact that around 20 percent of the land is waterlogged which is going to make sowing difficult," he said.
So far there had been more limited damage to crops such as strawberries, onions, asparagus and potatoes, although their worth in pesetas was still considerable, he said.
Orange crops had also been affected, although it was difficult to assess the extent of the damage.
The association was calling for aid from the government to offset the losses estimated, although as yet officials have been unable to survey the area.
Weather forecasts are predicting the rain will abate in the next few days, which should allow some recovery and official assessment.
